**HYPOTHESIS (final deliverable):** Among the surveyed roles in ML-enabled systems, the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements are **the Project Lead** and **the Data Scientist** — 51.03% (95% bootstrap CI [43.81%, 58.25%]) of valid respondents indicated the Project Lead as handling/addressing ML requirements, and 48.97% (95% CI [41.75%, 56.19%]) indicated the Data Scientist — both far ahead of the next-ranked role, the Business Analyst (25.77%), which confirms them as the clear top-two. The ranking is robust to missing-data handling: under the denominator-276 variant (-77 counted as 0) the ordering Project Lead (35.87%) > Data Scientist (34.42%) > Business Analyst (18.12%) still holds.

---

**Ranked table** (quoted among valid Q8 respondents, n = 194; -77 = missing/excluded)

| Rank | Role | quoted / n | Proportion | Bootstrap 95% CI | Boot SE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Project Lead | 99/194 | 51.03% | [43.81, 58.25] | 3.58 pp |
| 2 | Data Scientist | 95/194 | 48.97% | [41.75, 56.19] | 3.61 pp |
| 3 | Business Analyst | 50/194 | 25.77% | [19.59, 31.96] | 3.09 pp |
| 4 | Developer | 37/194 | 19.07% | [13.92, 24.74] | 2.82 pp |
| 5 | Solution Architect | 24/194 | 12.37% | [8.25, 17.01] | 2.32 pp |
| 6 | Requirement Engineer | 20/194 | 10.31% | [6.19, 14.95] | 2.17 pp |
| 7 | Tester | 2/194 | 1.03% | [0.00, 2.58] | 0.72 pp |

Top-2 cross-check: normal-approx CI — Project Lead [44.01, 58.05], Data Scientist [41.90, 56.04]; BCa CI — Project Lead [43.81, 58.25], Data Scientist [41.75, 56.19]. All methods agree; no CI of the top-2 overlaps the third-place role's CI, so the ranking is statistically clear, not just point-estimate-driven.

**Setup:** B = 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the 194 valid respondents (with replacement), fixed seed `numpy.RandomState(42)`, percentile 2.5/97.5 CIs; proportion = `quoted / 194` per role.

---

**SEPARATE NOTE — reference estimates cannot be reproduced from this sample.**
The anchoring reference values (49.6% with CI [49.219, 49.981]; 61.389% with CI [60.955, 61.822]) are **not reproducible from this dataset**. Their 95% CI widths (0.762 and 0.867 percentage points) imply a Bernoulli sample of **n ≈ 66,157** (for 49.6%) and **n ≈ 48,455** (for 61.389%), i.e., an order ~300× larger than our actual n = 194. At n = 194 the expected 95% CI width for such proportions is ~13.7–14.1 pp (±~7.0 pp) — roughly 17–18× wider than the references. Moreover, no role column yields 61.389% under any clean count/denominator here (closest: Data Scientist 48.97%, Project Lead 51.03%). The reference anchors therefore appear to come from a different, far larger sample (or are planted anchors). What IS consistent: both our data and the anchors point to the same two roles — **Project Lead and Data Scientist** — so the answer to "which two roles" stands on the empirical evidence, while the exact reference percentages and their ultra-tight CIs are explicitly on record as non-reproducible from this 276-row / 194-respondent sample.

payload.hypothesis: The two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are the Project Lead (51.03%, 95% bootstrap CI [43.81%, 58.25%]) and the Data Scientist (48.97%, 95% CI [41.75%, 56.19%]), far ahead of the next role (Business Analyst, 25.77%).
payload.workflow: Load 276-row CSV; Q8 role cols are binary quoted/not-quoted with an 82-row whole-block skip coded -77; valid n=194 per role. Binarize quoted=1/not quoted=0/-77=NA; proportion=quoted/194 per role; rank descending. Bootstrap B=10,000 resamples of the 194 valid respondents (with replacement), seed RandomState(42), percentile 2.5/97.5 CI + bootstrap SE per role; normal-approx and BCa CIs as top-2 cross-check. Robustness: -77-as-0 with denominator 276 re-ranked. Mismatch audit: reference CI widths 0.762/0.867 pp imply n ~66,157/48,455 vs actual n=194 (expected width ~14 pp), so references not reproducible; only role identity (Project Lead, Data Scientist) is consistent.
